scope: Only our method has been measured. Comparisons and ablations below are planned, not executed.
rules: Split by geometry/layout/sequence before development; new holdout after any feedback-based optimization.
Record planned cases, exclusions, source/configuration/binary hashes and random seeds before execution.
Keep all failures; separate arrivals from expected safe rejection and from flow qualification.
Do not count points, headings, masks, repeated room scans or CPU/GPU pairs as independent worlds.
Risk is an engineering score, not a calibrated event probability; height intervals and binary hazard detection are separate targets.
No external method run or GitHub push is authorized by this protocol alone.
Acceptance targets require supervisor/research approval; they must not be selected from favorable test results.

phases.target: Steps, gaps, cliffs, roof/overhang and vertical structures
phases.design: stratified boundary-focused subset; define finite combinations before running, not blind full Cartesian multiplication
phases.truth: independent dense 3D wheel/body clearance and support, not model risk

phases.target: Unknown terrain prediction without privileged ground labels
phases.source_split: new generated geometries plus held-out real off-road source groups; old public regression is not new evidence
phases.truth: complete independent reference used only for scoring, not GP input, selection, ground segmentation or thresholds

phases.target: Temporal maintenance and fast dynamic clearing
phases.observation: continue at least 3 seconds after goal arrival and at least 10 seconds after vacating

phases.layout_goal: at least 3 terrain categories and 10 independent layouts per major class, subject to data and simulator feasibility
phases.statistics: layout-cluster uncertainty; illustrative 299 IID zero-failure trials for a one-sided 95% failure upper bound below 1% is not satisfied by repeated same-layout tasks

matching: same raw inputs and held-out sources
equal tuning budget on validation only
phases.warning: Retain algorithm semantics. Engineering before/after tests are not external baselines; do not compare incompatible published risk scores directly.
